title: Tenor versus alto saxophone and transposing
summary: He preferred tenor to alto and read violin and alto parts easily, calling transposition a knack.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You know, it was a good band. I like tenor. I cut my teeth on alto, but I could never really control an alto. I never felt like I had an alto saxophone under control. It was an instrument of the devil, you know. But tenor, I got along very well with tenor. And I had enough musical background. In fact, at that time when tenor began, the tenor bands became very popular, I had no problem reading the alto parts, which is a transposition. As a matter of fact, I thank God I never had any trouble with any transposition. When I used to play the carnival ball with Tornel Luop, I used to read all the violin parts to reinforce the violin sections. I didn't play with the saxophone section. So you did a lot of transposing? Oh yeah. I didn't have any trouble, you know. It's one of those things that you either have a knack for or you don't. There's no secret to it. There's no great education to it. You have a fast eye and you have a fast ear and you get by. And a fast mind.
